After completion, it will be necessary to do a `git push --tags` if a commit and/or tag are created*** 9 10 ## Setup 11 12 auto-semver is a pip installable package to install, make sure pip is installed and simply run: 13 14 `pip install path/to/auto-semver-tar.gz` 15 16 ## Configuration 17 18 There is one configuration file that must appear in the top directory of repository for which we want to update the version, `.bumpversion.cfg`. 19 20 Below is an example configuration of a `.bumpversion.cfg` file: 21 22 ```ini 23 [bumpversion] 24 current_version = 0.0.0 25 commit = False 26 tag = True 27 tag_name = {new_version} 28 message = Bump version: {current_version} -> {new_version} 29 30 [bumpversion:file:VERSION] 31 search = version=0.0.0 32 replace = version={new_version} 33 34 [semver] 35 main_branches = master 36 major_branches = major 37 minor_branches = feature 38 patch_branches = hotfix, bugfix 39 ``` 40 41 ### bumpversion 42 43 ```ini 44 [bumpversion] 45 current_version = 0.0.0 46 commit = False 47 tag = True 48 tag_name = v{new_version} 49 message = Bump version: {current_version} -> {new_version} 50 ``` 51 52 The `current_version` exists to tell bumpversion what the current version is. Auto-semver uses this value as the default version if not version if found in the tags. The `commit` and `tag` options determine whether to create a new Git commit and a new Git tag, respectively. The `tag_name` represents what the name of the Git tag will be, and by default is set to `{new_version}`, which will be substitued with the new version during runtime. This can be changed as desired - for example, `v{new_version}` could resolve to `v1.15.5`. The `message` option is what the message used if there is a git commit. 53 54 ### File updates 55 56 ```ini 57 [bumpversion:file:VERSION] 58 search = version={current_version} 59 replace = version={new_version} 60 61 [bumpversion:file:example_app/__init__.py] 62 search = version = '{current_version}' 63 replace = version = '{new_version}' 64 ``` 65 66 The `search` and `replace` options describe how the tool will update the version in the `VERSION` file. The format must match the format of the contents of the `VERSION` file. The `{current_version}` represents the old version of the application and the `{new_version}` represents the version after it is updated. These will be substituted with the actual values at runtime. 67 68 You can use this to update mutiple files are runtime. 69 70 ### Branch Based Versioning 71 72 ```ini 73 [semver] 74 main_branches = master 75 major_branches = major 76 minor_branches = feature 77 patch_branches = hotfix, bugfix 78 ``` 79 80 The last four options are exceptionally important - they tie in to how the branching was done in the Git repository. Each one is expected to be a comma-delimited list. The `main_branches` option represents the Git branches that feature branches will be merged into. Functionally, the tool will make commits on the currently checked out branch during runtime, which must match one of the specified branches. 81 82 In order for the tool to make a determination on how to increment the version, it looks at the most recent commit, checks to determine if it was a merge from another branch, then compares the branch name to the values listed for the options. If the merged in branch name was prefixed with one of the values for `major_branches`, the major version number is incremented and the other numbers are set to 0. If the merged in branch name was prefixed with one of the values for `minor_branche`', the minor version number is incremented and the patch number is set to 0. If the merged in branch name was prefixed with one of the values for `patch_branches`, the patch number will be incremented. 83 84 Below is an example configuration in the VERSION file: 85 86 ```VERSION 87 version=1.15.5 88 ``` 89 90 The value for `version` represents the current version of the application, and should match the current_version in the `.bumpversion.cfg`. 91 92 ## Usage 93 94 95 #### semver 96 97 The `semver` command runs auto-semver in the current working directory. 98 99 The exit code of auto-semver determines the output. 100 101 **Exit codes**: 102 103 |Value|Meaning| 104 |---|---| 105 |0|Successfully ran auto-semver| 106 |1|No merge found| 107 |2|Not a main branch| 108 |3|No version branch name found| 109 |128|Unknown error occured| 110 111 #### Flags 112 113 `-n` 114 115 Does not push after versioning. 116 117 `-h` 118 119 Shows helps screen. 120 121 `-D`/`--debug` 122 123 Runs with debug logging. 124 125 126 ### semver_get_version 127 128 The `semver_get_version` command returns the version number if the `semver` command exited `0`. * This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.
